title: Primes of an integral algebra lift a geometric point
statement: Let $A\to C$ be an integral map of commutative rings, $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field, and $\phi:A\to\Omega$. For every prime $\mathfrak r$ of $C$ contracting to $\ker\phi$, there is a ring map $t:C\to\Omega$ extending $\phi$ with kernel $\mathfrak r$. Residue fields mean fraction fields of prime quotients [def-weil-residue-field].

proof.text: The map phi embeds the residue field at its kernel in Omega by the universal property of localization and fractions. Integrality implies that the residue extension at r is algebraic. Extend the embedding to this algebraic field extension inside the algebraically closed Omega. Compose with C to its residue field. The resulting map extends phi and has kernel r, since the map from the residue field to Omega is injective. This is the existing proof in GeometricPoint.lean:216-230, whose pinned sorry map is closed.
